newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Hewlett-Packard back in SAfrica after 8 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard back in SAfrica after 8 yrs.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co became the latest U.S. company to return to post-apartheid South Africa on Thursday with the planned acquisition of certain businesses of information technology group Siltek Ltd.
Siltek Ltd said earlier it had agreed to sell certain businesses and related assets of its HiPerformance Systems unit to Hewlett-Packard (HP).

HP first established a sales subsidiary in South Africa in 1968, growing it to annual sales of $62 million over the next 20 years. But the company pulled out of the country in 1989, selling its business to Siltek, citing political and economic uncertainties, and disappointment with the slow pace of social and economic change.

HP said the acquired operations would become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hewlett-Packard Europe. The deal includes those elements of HiPerformance involved with computer systems and solutions, professional services, test-and-measurement products and services, medical products and systems, and systems support operations.
Siltek will continue with the remaining business of HiPerformance, namely the distribution of HP chemical-analysis products and systems, maintenance of products and all operations in Botswana.
Around 250 employees will transfer to HP following the sale.
HP said it would use the deal to integrate the management of the distribution of its computer products and peripherals in South Africa.

"Changes in market and customer requirements, converging technologies and an improved political scene lead us to realise that a direct presence for HP is now more appropriate," said Bernard de Valence, general manager of HP International Sales Europe.
Siltek chairman Jack Saulez said both companies intended to develop future forms of cooperation.
The two companies said they expected the purchase price, payable in cash on November 1, to be based on the tangible net asset value of the businesses as at October 31, plus a payment for goodwill.

"The proceeds of the disposal, including HiPerformance surplus cash retained by Siltek and commission on future sales, cannot be precisely quantified at this stage but is estimated to be of the order of 200 million rand," the companies said in a statement.
